description: MATCHING-DESIGN.md sections 3.2 to 3.15 and 4 (with section 5's per-chain parameters and section 14's provisional names): the shared ranking algorithm and its test vectors. Ranking: the list of a round (4.4), its schedule, list hash and turns (4.5), the three examples of 3.8 and the raise of 3.15; paging: candidates pages with the carried hash and matchFound (4.5, 4.6); charges: the miss predicate of 4.8 with mandateOutcomes and the ballot; windows: the members' full-window test of 3.12; sequences: the contract's arithmetic of 4.9 (claims, the settlement at the heartbeat, apply and giveBack under the per-slot cap, recordMisses, the recount, askCorrection and correct, failed orders, strikes, the ban, the two switches); approvals: the runner's default rule of 3.10; quotes: bidQuote and bidQuoteFor (4.6). spec/matching.md states every rule; spec/make/matching-rank.js computes every expected value.

encoding.roundStamp: keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint256 doRequestId, bytes22 seedStamp, uint8 round, uint48 roundBlock, uint32 roundTime, uint128 bid, uint128 base)): 97 bytes
encoding.listHash: h0 = bytes32(0); h = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(bytes32 h, address node, uint8 flags)), flags = fit + 2 x match: 53 bytes per link
encoding.seedStamp: the first (high-order) 22 bytes of the parent block hash: bytes22(blockhash(block.number - 1))
encoding.eligibleWord: uint160(node) << 96 | uint16(score) << 80 | fit << 73 | match << 72 | uint24(listedOrdinal) << 48 | uint48(dpRequestId)
encoding.claimSteps: uint24 steps: round r in bits 4r to 4r + 3
encoding.maxGflopsArg: the V2 add's uint48 maxGflops: the minimum EPC in units of 64 MiB in bits 32 to 47 (D191, 0: any), required CU in GFLOPS in bits 16 to 31, the ceiling in bits 0 to 15
encoding.gflopsArg: the V2 offer's uint40 gflops (D167, D191): GFLOPS in bits 0 to 15, the enclave memory in GiB in bits 16 to 23, the EPC in units of 64 MiB in bits 24 to 39 (0: none)
encoding.correctionEntry: kind << 248; kinds 1 and 6: | uint48(doRequestId) << 16 | uint8(round) << 8 | uint8(step); kinds 2 to 4: | uint48(orderId); kind 5: | uint32(slot)
encoding.imageKey: bytes31(keccak256(bytes(field 1 of metadata1))): the first 31 bytes

charges.name: raise-late-not-absent-round-1

charges.name: earlier-round-claim-answers-round-0

charges.name: false-approved-lower

sequences.name: settle-late-claim
sequences.design: 4.9: a claim in time adds no pending entry; a late claim stays pending while its request is open and is charged at the first heartbeat once it is filled

sequences.name: cancel-before-charge
sequences.design: 4.9, D58: a late claim on a request cancelled without an approval stays while the request is younger than 24 hours and is dropped with no charge after

sequences.name: cancel-after-charge
sequences.design: 4.9: the first recorded charge marks the request judged; a cancel after it changes nothing for the next node

sequences.name: two-rounds-one-claim
sequences.design: 4.9, 3.15: a claim mined in round 1 states steps for rounds 0 and 1; both are charged at one heartbeat, inside the cap of the request's slot (1,644 + 548 -> 1,918)

sequences.name: own-blocks-no-charge
sequences.design: 4.9: the approval's own blocks: B (stated 1) claimed in step 1, A (stated 3) late in step 4, B approved after: no charge, the entry leaves without counting toward settleMax

sequences.name: false-hides-late-step
sequences.design: 4.9 recordMisses: A (real step 1) stated 0 and claimed late: no pending entry; the ballot's FALSE entry charges 1,918 and ends its period

sequences.name: false-over-settled-late
sequences.design: 4.9: A (real 1) stated 2 and claimed in step 3; its heartbeat settles 548; the ballot's FALSE entry then charges 1,918 - 548 = 1,370 and moves the count from lates to misses

sequences.name: false-before-settled-late
sequences.design: 4.9: the same statement with the ballot first: 1,918; the heartbeat after it finds the record and charges nothing

sequences.name: approved-states-lower
sequences.design: 4.9: the approved B (real 3) stated 1; A (stated 2) late, settled on fill step 1 at 548; the ballot writes step 3, charges B a FALSE 1,918 and recounts A upward to 1,096

sequences.name: approved-states-higher
sequences.design: 4.9: the approved B (real 1) stated 3; A (stated 2) late, settled on fill step 3 at 1,096; the ballot writes step 1 and charges B; A's kind-6 entry recounts it down to 0 with no vote

sequences.name: approved-from-earlier-round
sequences.design: 4.9: B's claim of round 0 is approved in round 1 (fill step 0); C (stated 3) late in round 1, settled at 548; the ballot cast for the step alone writes 2; C's kind-6 entry recounts to 0

sequences.name: earlier-round-claim-entry-skipped
sequences.design: 4.9 recordMisses: B's claim of round 0 is approved in round 1; a ballot of round 1 that names B with step 2 is skipped for it, since a claim mined in an earlier round answers the round; the ballot writes the fill step 2

sequences.name: approved-in-claim-block
sequences.design: 4.9 recordMisses, 3.12: A claims in step 1 stating 1 and is approved in the block of its claim; a ballot that names A with real step 0 and approvedStep 1 records no charge: the statement is the fill record's step

sequences.name: approved-states-neither
sequences.design: 4.9 recordMisses, 3.12 case (2): A claims in step 1 stating 3 and is approved in the block of its claim; the ballot names A with real step 0 and approvedStep 1: the statement is neither, a FALSE record of 1,918 with step 0, and its period is not ended

sequences.name: earlier-step-stated
sequences.design: 4.9: A (real 3) states 1 and claims in step 3: the contract charges 1,096 on its word

sequences.name: excused-states-zero
sequences.design: 4.9: a node whose mandate was excused states 0: no pending entry, no charge

sequences.name: recount-up-keeps-undone
sequences.design: 4.9, O89: A (stated 2) late in step 5, settled on fill step 1 at 1,096 (steps 2 and 3); its step 2 undone (548 back); the ballot writes step 3 and recounts A upward over steps 2 to 4 less the undone one, 1,096; a later ask of step 2 is refused as undone

sequences.name: recount-down-keeps-undone
sequences.design: 4.9, O89: A (stated 2) late in step 5, settled on fill step 3 at 1,644; its step 2 undone (548 back); the ballot writes step 1; A's kind-6 entry recounts it over step 2 alone, which is undone: 0, 1,096 back

sequences.name: bound-one-a-heartbeat
sequences.design: D176, 4.9: with settleMax 1 (bloxberg) three final late claims are charged at three heartbeats, one each, each walk resuming at the first entry not examined

sequences.name: bound-two-a-heartbeat
sequences.design: D176, 4.9: with settleMax 2 (Amoy's set, 12-block steps) three final late claims are charged two at the first heartbeat and the third at the next

sequences.name: bound-carry-past-ballot
sequences.design: D176 effect 1, the fill record: A's late claim on X is carried past X's ballot, which writes the approved C's real step 1 over its stated 3; the next heartbeat counts A on that fill step and A leaves with no charge, where a settlement before the ballot counts 1,644 on the stated step until A's kind-6 entry (approved-states-higher)

sequences.name: bound-carry-past-cancel
sequences.design: D176 effect 2, a cancel: two late claims on requests left unfilled past their 24 hours; the first heartbeat charges one, the data owner cancels the other before any charge, and the next heartbeat drops it with no charge (D58)

sequences.name: bound-carry-past-ban
sequences.design: D176 effect 3, a ban: two final late claims; the first heartbeat charges one; a ban then empties the pending list and the carried claim is never charged

sequences.name: bound-carry-window
sequences.design: D176 effect 4, the correction window: two final late claims charged at two heartbeats an hour apart; a kind-1 ask 24 hours and 100 seconds after the first is outside the first record's window and inside the carried one's, which counts from its own charge

sequences.name: bound-carry-floor
sequences.design: D176 effect 5, the score's floor and the slot gain: a node at 300 units with two final late claims on requests of two slots; the first heartbeat's gain takes it to 437 and the first charge to 0; the carried charge takes the next heartbeat's gain, 137, so the node ends at 0, where both charges at one heartbeat leave it at 137 after the next gain

sequences.name: correction-kind-1
sequences.design: 3.12, 4.9 kind 1: a late charge of two steps, one undone: 548 back; one of five steps undone: nothing back; a second list inside the hour refused; an entry after the window skipped

sequences.name: correction-under-cap
sequences.design: 3.12, 4.9: a late charge (548) and a failed order (1,918) on requests of one slot take 1,918 (548, then 1,370); undoing the late step gives nothing back; undoing the failed order after it gives back all 1,918

sequences.name: correction-kinds-2-to-5
sequences.design: 3.12, 4.9 kinds 2 to 5: a never-started order, an expired order, a node fault on code 37 and a lost heartbeat slot, each given back; a node fault on code 40 is not correctable

sequences.name: two-failures-one-slot-both-corrected
sequences.design: 3.12, 4.9 kinds 2 to 4: two never-started orders on requests of one slot; the first takes the cap's 1,918 and the second nothing; both corrected in one ballot: the first gives nothing back while the second's units cover the cap, the second gives the 1,918 back; no failed order is counted and lastFailureSlot is cleared

sequences.name: two-failures-one-slot-one-stands
sequences.design: 3.12, 4.9 kinds 2 to 4: the same two failures; the second, which took no units, corrected alone: nothing back, one failed order still counted and lastFailureSlot kept, since the first names the slot; the first corrected after it: 1,918 back and lastFailureSlot cleared

sequences.name: heartbeat-correction-after-ban
sequences.design: 3.12, 3.17, 4.9 kind 5: a node with no heartbeat in a slot sends one in the next slot and is banned after it; the slot's entry is skipped at the ask and at the vote, since the slot did not end after the ban's end: the gain is not added to the score the ban set to 0

sequences.name: correction-after-heartbeats-ban-and-cap
sequences.design: 4.9 giveBack: units added to the score as it stands after further heartbeats; nothing given back after a ban; nothing above 50,000

sequences.name: rotation-full-list
sequences.design: 4.9, D96: sixteen pending claims, five open at the head; each heartbeat charges at most four final entries from where the last stopped; a seventeenth pending claim is refused, an in-time one admitted

sequences.name: cap-two-requests
sequences.design: 3.12, D18: absences on two requests of one slot: 1,918 taken once; a strike recorded in a later slot is charged in its own slot

sequences.name: score-floor-and-cap
sequences.design: 4.9 apply: the cap counts the sum of the charges, not what the floor of 0 let be taken: a node at 500 loses 500 to a missed mandate and nothing to a later late charge of the same slot

sequences.name: switches
sequences.design: 3.4, 3.14: the heartbeat that first takes a node to 10,000 sets minimumOnAt and the one that first takes a node to 45,000 sets farmMinOnAt; later crossings write nothing

approvals.name: approve-n1-in-step
approvals.design: 3.8 Example 1 row 1: N1's claim of block 1002 is approved at the read of 1002

approvals.name: approve-n5-after-n1-closed
approvals.design: 3.8 Example 1 row 2: at the read of 1002 N1's step is closed without its claim: N5 approved

approvals.name: in-time-before-late

approvals.name: late-when-no-in-time

approvals.name: early-waits-for-n2
approvals.design: 3.8 Example 1 row 5: N3 claimed early in 1003; at the read of 1003 N2's step is not closed: wait

approvals.name: early-approved-after-n2
approvals.design: 3.8 Example 1 row 5: at the read of 1004 N2's step is closed: N3 approved
